restrictions: Generic distinguished-point birthday collision search on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family; no cryptanalytic weakness in 40-round SHA-256 is claimed and no full-width 256-bit collision is produced.
Full-width success probability (>= 0.390000001) relies on H1-random-function-walk under the declared collision-frontier-v5 256-bit word-RAM model.

heuristics.statement: The iterated 256-bit Walk-B transition F(Y) = B(Y) XOR PD on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family of 40-round SHA-256 behaves like a uniform random function on {0,1}^256 with respect to birthday collision hazard, distinguished-point hitting times (p = 2704 / 2^122), trail-length tails, and 37-bit key independence.
heuristics.scope: Complete 40-round SHA-256 (steps 0..39 on every padded block, standard FIPS 180-4 IV, padding, message schedule, and feed-forward) restricted to 64-byte messages with fixed 8-word prefix W[0..7] and affine offsets W[8+k] = Y_k - K[8+k] (k=2..7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Extrapolated from the van Oorschot-Wiener (1999) and Flajolet-Odlyzko (1990) random-function birthday theory together with two organizer-executed reduced-width experiments on the exact 64-byte W[0..7]-prefix family at w=16 (bounded DP collision recovery) and w=14 (fixed-budget M=127 collision rate near P=0.39).
heuristics.limitations: Empirical reduced-width experiments at w=16 and w=14 cannot prove the absence of structural correlations or non-random cycle behavior at full 256-bit width. If 40-round SHA-256 deviated significantly from a random function under F, the achieved success probability could fall below 0.39.
